The line: I have watched every Age end, and written down what each one cost.
How to say it: Level and unhurried; the weight on "cost"

The line: Whoever sits on that Throne rules every other god, and decides where the rain falls.
How to say it: Plain, a fact; a little slower on "where the rain falls"

The line: To end their wars, the first gods carved the Covenant into the sky. It didn't end them. It scheduled them.
How to say it: Even through "sky", then a beat; the last two sentences dry, almost amused, with a small pause between them

The line: One god rules for one Age: two thousand years. And nobody asked the world below whether it agreed.
How to say it: Read like the terms of a contract; the last sentence quieter

The line: This Age belongs to Solmaris, and the sun has kept perfect time.
How to say it: Calm; a shade too smooth on "perfect time"
Slow and final; the weight on "due"

The line: The other six would like her gone.
How to say it: Understated, no menace in the voice; the pictures do that

The line: Gods can break the sky, but not each other. So they spend the living instead.
How to say it: Flat; no push on "spend", let the word do it

The line: Their magic has always spilled into the world below,
How to say it: Unhurried; it runs straight on into 09b, so end it open, not falling
Picks up from 09a; plain, almost ordinary

The line: Kingdoms were built on cards. Now they fight with them, not swords. Fewer die that way. I notice the difference.
How to say it: Brisk to "swords", then slower; "I notice the difference" almost to herself

The line: Each kingdom has a Champion, marked by a god. Anyone may challenge one for the mark. The last one standing crowns their god.
How to say it: Plain and level, like rules read aloud

The line: And in Ironvault, a man who holds half the world in debt has started to ask what the gods are for.
How to say it: Lower, with a note of interest, as if this one is worth watching

The line: On the last night of the Age, over a village that had hung its lanterns anyway...
...the Covenant marked an eighth Champion, and left the god's name blank.
How to say it: Quiet; a small pause after "Champion", and the last four words very quiet
